column1: # Classes of the open MUST rows, read by scripts/open-must.py, which writes OPEN-MUST.md.
# One line per row: ID, class, size, owner, what would close it (tab-separated). Classes:
#   A  RFC behaviour implemented and tested, a named setting, not the default because a named
#      browser cell or deployed peer cannot interoperate, or a named repository test measured
#   B  implemented, lacking a test that fails without it
#   C  partly implemented (the close column says what is missing)
#   E  cannot be met or observed inside this engine for the stated reason
#   F  the note is stale: the behaviour is already tested on this tree
# Owner "(running)" marks a row another agent's branch owns now; it is listed, not worked.
# A row closed since it was classified (tested / n/a) is reported by --check as stale.

Tested (default provider ring, optimised build, x86-64 Linux with the oldest supported compiler and stable, AArch64 macOS, CI job key_residue): no key an SRTP session derives is found in any form in the dead stack frames of the thread after building, packets, re-keying or tearing down, nor (Linux) anywhere else in the process after the teardown; either provider, unoptimised and optimised builds, the same compilers: building and tearing down leave nothing on the stack (the overwrite is 128 KiB deep unoptimised, 32 KiB optimised) and every heap copy is erased. Not met or not shown: the AWS-LC provider's packet path leaves HMAC-SHA1 states and a GHASH table entry in dead stack frames for every packet (its own frames; known_limit_with_aws_lc_the_packet_path_leaves_keys_in_dead_stack_frames, ignored); the packet path of a build with `debug_assertions` off for rtci-crypto but `aes` unoptimised; CPU registers and what saves them (signal frames, lazy thread-local set-up); Windows and other architectures not measured; a provider deeper than the overwrite. DTLS (measured, zeroize-5): no secret of key derivation in a dead stack frame after any step, either provider, every build and compiler measured; not shown: the record path (ring ChaCha20-Poly1305 per record, AWS-LC GHASH / HMAC-SHA1), AES-CCM below rustc 1.99.1 optimised (1 to 3 round keys), IVs; the unoptimised record path is overwritten (dtls-34) and asserted. Unproven for both: registers and signal frames, the Windows stack (heap side only), AWS-LC internals.
